tools.name: search_food
tools.title: Search foods
tools.description: Search Cronometer's food database. Returns an array of foods: name, id (pass as food_id to log_food), measureId and measureDisplayName (the default serving, e.g. "1 medium - 118g"; pass measureId as measure_id with amount 1 for one of that serving), source (NCCDB, USDA, CRDB, brand databases) and type (FOOD, RECIPE).

tools.name: get_diary
tools.title: Read food diary
tools.description: Everything logged on one day (GWT-RPC text, read it as data). Each food serving carries its serving id (a short quoted string like "FAoVo9"; pass it to delete_diary_entry), the food id, the measure id, the amount and the day. Biometrics and notes for the day appear too. Food names are not included: match food ids against search_food results.

tools.name: get_daily_nutrition
tools.title: Daily nutrition totals
tools.description: Total nutrients consumed on one day (GWT-RPC text). Values are keyed by Cronometer nutrient id: 208 energy kcal, 203 protein g, 205 carbs g, 204 fat g, 291 fiber g, 304 magnesium mg, 303 iron mg, 324 vitamin D IU, 307 sodium mg, 301 calcium mg, 401 vitamin C mg. Compare with get_targets for the same ids.

tools.name: get_targets
tools.title: Nutrient targets
tools.description: The user's daily nutrient targets: an array of {id, min, max, vis}. id is the Cronometer nutrient id: 208 energy kcal, 203 protein g, 205 carbs g, 204 fat g, 291 fiber g, 304 magnesium mg, 303 iron mg, 324 vitamin D IU, 307 sodium mg (max is the upper limit), 301 calcium mg, 401 vitamin C mg, 255 water g.

tools.name: log_food
tools.title: Log food
tools.description: Add one serving to the diary. Get food_id (id) and measure_id (measureId) from search_food. amount counts the chosen measure: 1 with the default measure is one serving (1 medium banana); with a gram measure it is grams. Returns GWT-RPC text whose first quoted string is the new serving id (pass it to delete_diary_entry).

meal.description: Diary group code: 65537 Breakfast, 131073 Lunch, 196609 Dinner, 262145 Snacks, 1 Uncategorized

tools.name: delete_diary_entry
tools.title: Remove diary entry
tools.description: Delete one food serving from the diary by its serving id (the short quoted string from log_food or get_diary, e.g. "FAoVo9", without the quotes). Returns //OK on success.

playbook: Open https://cronometer.com/login/ in the in-app browser and sign in with email and password
Wait for https://cronometer.com/ to load the web app (script cronometer.nocache.js present, diary date arrows visible)

Visit /#diary and step the diary one day back and forward so the app sends getDayInfo; read the session nonce (lowercase 32-hex string in the GWT body), the GWT policy hash (body field 5), the X-GWT-Permutation request header and the user id (/api/v3/user/<id>/ in REST URLs) off those requests
Open Add Food, type a search (GET /api/v3/user/<id>/food-search/string), then close the dialog without adding
Leave the app page: park the relay WebView on https://cronometer.com/about/ (static). Reloading / re-runs authenticate and rotates the nonce; loading /login/ kills it

provenance.notes: Verified live 2026-11-15 on matt's account with scripts/re/cronometer/client.ts (device path: requests run from a signed-in cronometer.com/about/ page with cookies): auth.check, search_food, get_targets, get_diary and get_daily_nutrition pass; log_food logged 1 medium Banana, Fresh to Snacks (serving FFD66t), get_diary showed it, delete_diary_entry returned //OK[[],0,7], get_diary showed it gone. Two transports: GWT-RPC POST /cronometer/app (text/x-gwt-rpc, session nonce as the first string arg; works from Node with no cookies, so the nonce acts as a bearer) and JSON REST /api/v3/user/{id}/* (cookie only, 401 from Node without cookies). Hence executor device. Nonce rotates on every web-app page load (authenticate) and dies when /login/ is loaded while signed in. GWT policy hash and permutation change on Cronometer deploys; they are taken from the session so a re-capture heals them. Type signatures (Serving/2895043750, AddEntryChange/3949104564, Day/782579793, DayQueryType/1802942352) matched the current web JS. updateDiary body copied from the web app's own request (sent blocked, then replayed through the template); meal code is (diary group << 16) | 1, group 4 = Snacks seen live, 1-3 assumed Breakfast/Lunch/Dinner. get_daily_nutrition (getTotalNutrients) is built from the web client's proxy signature, not seen in a UI flow; its map uses GWT back-references once foods are logged, so ids are not all literal: readable totals are an open item (decoder or the /export dailySummary CSV, which needs a generateAuthorizationToken step first). Sources: jrmycanady/gocronometer and cphoskins/cronometer-mcp (web GWT + export); mobile-API projects deliberately not used.
